metadata.title: Why can’t I enter this directory?
metadata.topic: Linux directories · read versus search permissions

mission.brief: You own the Research folder. You can list its names but cannot enter it or read the note inside. Keep private owner name-listing access and restore only the traversal access needed to enter Research and read welcome.txt. The ancestors are accessible and the note already has owner-read permission.
constraints: Required final mode of /home/learner/Research: owner read and execute (0500), no write and no group/other access. Preserve the existing name-listing permission. 0700 and 0777 grant unnecessary access and fail the mode objective.

Verification: successfully enter Research and read Research/welcome.txt after the most recent actual permission change. Order and equivalent supported paths are flexible. No initial failed command is required for credit.
Only the Research directory has editable mode bits. Ancestors, note permissions, ownership and file contents are fixed. Changes take effect immediately.

Directory read permission allows name listing; execute allows search/traversal and access to known children. This simulation supports names-only ls with read permission. ls -l needs read plus execute for child metadata and reports a clear error rather than partial metadata rows. Inspect Research itself with a long listing of its accessible parent.
This is a bounded virtual environment. No real shell, file, process, network or chmod is used. No recursive changes, links, ACLs or full Linux command emulation. Help documents the exact syntax.

objectives.label: Final mode: retain private listing and add traversal only
Verification: enter Research after the last mode change
Verification: read welcome.txt after the last mode change

hints: A directory’s read and execute bits do different jobs. Listing a name does not guarantee you can enter the directory or open that child.
The directory already has owner-read permission. Its missing owner-execute bit blocks traversal; the note’s own read permission is already correct.
Add only owner-execute with chmod u+x Research, or set mode 500. Then enter Research and read welcome.txt. 777 and 700 give write or other access that this goal does not need.

/etc/motd.content: Learning Lab: a small simulated filesystem.

/root/private.txt.content: This virtual file is reserved for the simulated root user.

/home/learner/Research/welcome.txt.content:
Welcome to Research.
Directory read permission lets you list names.
Directory execute permission lets you enter and access known children.
The file also needs its own read permission.

lesson.goal: Keep Research private: list its names, restore traversal, enter it and read the welcome note.

steps.explanation: Inspect the parent’s long listing. For the Research directory, owner r permits listing names. The missing owner x blocks traversal. Group and other have no access.
steps.expected: Research appears with dr--------, owned by learner.

steps.explanation: Plain ls lists names using directory read permission. Seeing a name does not mean you can enter the folder or open that file.
steps.expected: welcome.txt is listed, even though Research still lacks execute permission.

steps.explanation: Try entering Research. Directory x means search/traversal, not running the directory as a program. Read alone is not enough.
steps.expected: Permission denied. Your current directory does not change.

steps.explanation: Add only owner x; keep owner r. Numeric 500 also means owner read (4) plus execute (1). Write is unnecessary, and 777 exposes the folder to other people.
steps.expected: Mode 0500. Owner can list and traverse; nobody gets write or group/other access.

steps.explanation: Enter the repaired directory to verify traversal. This records evidence without prescribing how you reached the parent.
Now read the note. Reaching a file requires search permission along its directory path and read permission on the file itself.
steps.expected: The note begins Welcome to Research. Submit when ready.
